body:
[As I commented on the Godot Developers Chat](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/web?msg=gWxqf5qr4YNrmz5Pb), I don't like the idea of modifying the behaviour for every platform (the PR edits scene/main/viewport.cpp) just to fix an issue on the Web platform.

The problem lies deeper with the implementation of the virtual keyboard, and how Godot handles such queries. I don't think it's a Web-specific problem per se.

The issue doesn't appear on hardware keyboard because Godot registers every keyboard event as Godot Input event.The problem with virtual keyboards is that they don't necessarily give such "keyboard events". 

They just say that the input changed, sometimes describing what they did. But it's not necessarily 1-to-1 with keyboard events, especially when autocorrecting words (as the input can delete some characters and insert new ones).

As a result, what the code does is to replace completely the text field with the contents of the new input. Then pressing "Right" as much times its needed to get the cursor at the end of the textfield.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8b2739ee55f8bebe7c4a20c55841851c4f411efe/platform/web/display_server_web.cpp#L797-L813

Quite hacky.

The problem lies in the fact that replacing a text field text (i.e. `LineEdit.set_text()`) doesn't trigger the `text_changed` signal. And changing this behavior unexpectedly would introduce a TON of bugs in users projects.

The quick solution would be to test if the actual text was changed (by comparing the value of the text before [`ds->input_text_callback.call(p_text);`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8b2739ee55f8bebe7c4a20c55841851c4f411efe/platform/web/display_server_web.cpp#L798). But I don't know how easily we can do it yet.
